newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares mixed again in heavier PSE trading.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares mixed again in heavier PSE trading.

text.p: Major Czech issues closed mixed for the second consecutive session on the Prague Stock Exchange in heavier trading on Wednesday as the bourse returned to its slumping ways.
The PX50 index fell 6.0 points, or 1.17 percent, to 508.6 while the Reuters RPIX index dropped 16.3 points to 1,042.2.

SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka -- the bourse's three most-capitalised issues -- all lost ground, but several others including bank Ceska Sporitelna, confectioner Cokoladovny recouped losses from Tuesday.
Overall, 177 stocks rose, 143 fell and 66 traded unchanged. Total volume was heavier at 1.77 million shares on turnover of 2.0 billion crowns.
A strong showing by the governing coalition in weekend Senate elections and a technical rally had broken the bourse from a two-month downturn that saw it lose some 17 percent.
But analysts said the PSE had, as expected, lost its momentum, and could begin another, though less dramatic fall to year-end.
"There may be some price rises as year-end accounting moves artifically boost some issues, but I doubt we will see any significant moves," said one local broker.
On the broader market, glass fibre maker Vertex, against market expectations, gained 167 crown to close at 3,511.
